tests_that_prove_nothing: Minor, the code is correct. The ENABLE_PRICE_PARSE_OFFLOAD gate on the curl_fetch_html cap is only ever tested with the value 'true'. Mutant N_curl_cap_flag_true_only_literal gates the cap on `os.getenv('ENABLE_PRICE_PARSE_OFFLOAD') == 'true'` instead of price_parse_offload_enabled(). It SURVIVED the whole of tests/test_retro_w0_4.py (157 passed). With the flag set to '1', 'yes' or 'on', that mutant still offloads but no longer caps, and no test would notice. The fixer's accepted-values pin (test_w04c_site_offloads_under_every_accepted_flag_value) covers only the six W0-4c sites, not the curl cap or the render-leg cap.

Minor, the code is correct. test_w04c_extract_with_ai_sends_the_same_prompt_flag_on_vs_off uses a fixture page whose visible text is far under 4,000 chars. Mutant N_ues_text_trunc_on truncates text_content to 3,999 chars after the flag-ON offload only. It SURVIVED (157 passed), so flag-ON prompt identity is not pinned for pages that reach the 4,000-char truncation. The fixer's two named mutants (the title/text swap in either branch) and N_ues_title_blank_on are killed.

Minor, harness only. scripts/verify_flag_byte_identity.py compare_results has a docstring that promises 'either side missing counts', but nothing pins it. Mutant N_harness_compare_intersection_only counts differing records over the key intersection only. It SURVIVED tests/test_verify_flag_byte_identity.py (19 passed). If the other payload is missing records, the output would read 'DIFFERING RECORDS 0 of N' next to equal=False. The exit status is still 1, because it follows the results digest, which is pinned.

Minor, harness only. Nothing pins what --compare does when the other file has no 'results' key. The code defaults to an empty list, which makes the comparison unequal. Mutant N_harness_compare_whole_payload_not_results defaults to this run's own results instead, so comparing against a wrong or non-payload JSON passes as equal=True with exit 0. It SURVIVED (19 passed).

Not gaps, recorded for completeness. Two survivors are equivalent in production: N_sem_size_check_removed (drops `held[1] != size` from _get_price_parse_semaphore) and N_pool_size_read_every_call (sizes the semaphore from price_parse_max_workers() instead of pool._max_workers). The pool is built once per process and PRICE_PARSE_MAX_WORKERS does not change at runtime, so the two sizes cannot diverge.
